title: Finance Assistant
company: Get Staffed Online Recruitment Limited - Agency - Permanent
description:
Finance Assistant

Part-Time: 16 hours per week; flexible working pattern to suit you

Clifton from early 2027 (until then this role will be based in our client's Bath office)

An exciting opportunity has arisen within the finance team of a well-established group of companies. Our client is looking for an experienced, part-time Finance Assistant to support the Finance Manager across the group.

Building on the purchase ledger function, this role also takes on subcontractors' CIS invoicing and bank reconciliations across the group, offering real variety and scope to develop within the finance team.

This role would suit someone with solid experience in purchase ledger, bookkeeping or accounts payable, together with a good understanding of the Construction Industry Scheme (CIS) and confidence managing bank reconciliations across multiple companies. Experience with Sage Line 50 is required and knowledge of Eque 2 Construct is highly beneficial, as is a background in construction or property.

This is a permanent, part-time position, based in a Bath office initially, moving to a new Clifton office when it opens in early 2027.

What's In It For You:
- Flexible working pattern to suit you.
- 16 hours per week.
- Workplace pension scheme.
- 28 days holiday, pro rata, plus an extra day for your birthday.
- Brand new office with a free gym and break out spaces opening in Clifton Village in early 2027.

Key Responsibilities:
- Processing supplier and subcontractor purchase invoices on Eque 2 Construct and Sage Line 50.
- Verifying subcontractor CIS status and applying the correct CIS deduction.
- Supporting the preparation of the monthly CIS returns and issuing subcontractor statements.
- Collating creditor payment runs and issuing remittances.
- Checking supplier and subcontractor statements and resolving queries.
- Reconciling bank accounts, credit cards and petty cash across the group of companies.
- Liaising with the wider finance team, subcontractors and suppliers.

Skills Required:
- An accounting qualification at a minimum AAT Level 2 Accounting or above is essential.
- Proven experience (3+ years) in purchase ledger, accounts payable or bookkeeping is essential.
- Good working knowledge of Sage Line 50 is essential.
- Experience of Eque 2 Construct is beneficial.
- An understanding of CIS and reverse charge VAT is required.
- Experience in working with a variety of costs centres and VAT rates.
- Strong Microsoft Office skills, particularly Excel.
- Highly organised and accurate, able to work independently and to deadlines.
- Comfortable working in a small team.
- Excellent communication skills and strong mathematical skills.

Apply now with a CV, and to really stand out, submit a Cover Letter as well.

title: Finance Assistant
company: Hays Specialist Recruitment Limited - Agency - Permanent
description:
Your new company:

Hays Accountancy & Finance are partnering exclusively with a growing and forward-thinking finance services organisation based in Cheltenham, Gloucestershire to recruit an experienced permanent Finance Assistant. This is an exciting opportunity to join a progressive business that provides high-quality finance support to a varied portfolio of growing organisations. You will work as part of a collaborative client services team, gaining exposure to different businesses while helping clients improve their financial processes, systems and ways of working.

The organisation embraces technology, automation and continuous improvement, making this an excellent opportunity for an experienced Finance Assistant who enjoys working in a fast-paced, modern finance environment. The position offers remote/office hybrid working of 2 days on-site, 3 days remote, flexible working hours, company/personal annual bonus scheme, development opportunities, study package for AAT if applicable, private healthcare and more.

Your new role:

Reporting to the wider client services team, you will work directly with a portfolio of clients, ensuring accurate financial records are maintained while supporting the implementation and improvement of processes and technology.

Key responsibilities will include:
- Processing sales transactions from sales order through to invoicing and receipt, ensuring a high level of accuracy.
- Processing purchase transactions from requisition and purchase order through to invoice and payment.
- Working as part of the client engagement team to support the onboarding of new clients.
- Supporting the implementation of standardised finance processes and automation tools.
- Building strong working relationships with clients to ensure the correct information is obtained and transactions are processed accurately.
- Helping clients adopt new processes, systems and ways of working.
- Working with the wider team to identify and implement improvements that increase accuracy, efficiency and the overall service delivered to clients.

What you'll need to succeed:

To be considered for this hands-on Finance Assistant position, you will ideally be AAT qualified or equivalent, with practical transactional finance experience.
- Previous experience using accounting software such as Xero and/or Sage.
- Intermediate Microsoft Excel skills.
- A good understanding of sales and purchase ledger processes.
- Experience or confidence in using AI-based tools and automation to improve finance processes, reconciliations, data entry or reporting.
- Strong attention to detail with a process-driven approach.
- The ability to work independently and manage competing priorities.
- Excellent communication skills with the ability to explain financial information clearly.
- Strong organisation and time-management skills.
- A proactive and adaptable approach with the ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced and changing environment.
- A genuine interest in continuous improvement, technology and developing more efficient ways of working.
- Multi-client experience would be advantageous but not essential.

You will be a collaborative and commercially minded individual who enjoys building trusted relationships with both clients and colleagues. You will take ownership of your work, be comfortable working at pace and enjoy being part of a growing organisation.

What you'll get in return

This permanent Finance Assistant position offers the opportunity to join an ambitious and growing finance services organisation in Cheltenham, Gloucestershire with exposure to a diverse portfolio of clients and businesses. Salary of £28,000 - £34,000 per annum, dependable on experience with up to a 10 % personal/company annual bonus.

The role offers a flexible working arrangement of two days on-site, three days remote, flexible working hours, private health care, critical illness cover, group income protection, development opportunities, study package for AAT if required and more. It is an excellent opportunity if you are looking to join a modern environment where technology, automation, client service and continuous improvement are central to the organisation.

What you need to do now

If you're interested in this role, click 'apply now' to forward an up-to-date copy of your CV, or call us now. If this job isn't quite right for you, but you are looking for a new position, please contact us for a confidential discussion about your career.

title: Service Advisor
description:
Service Advisor

Cheltenham £28,000 Basic Salary £33,000 OTE

Good Service Advisors make a busy workshop feel effortless.

We're looking for an experienced Service Advisor to join an established automotive dealership in Cheltenham.

You'll be at the centre of the customer journey, working closely with the workshop to keep vehicles moving, customers informed and expectations managed from the moment a vehicle is booked in through to collection.

If you know your way around a busy aftersales department, enjoy working with people and take pride in getting the details right, we'd like to talk.

The opportunity

This is a customer-facing role with plenty of variety. You'll be managing several vehicles and customer conversations throughout the day, balancing customer expectations with workshop capacity and making sure everyone knows what's happening.

You'll be responsible for:
- Booking vehicles into the workshop and understanding exactly what the customer needs
- Preparing accurate job cards and making sure the right information is captured from the outset
- Liaising closely with Technicians, Workshop Controllers and the wider aftersales team
- Providing clear estimates and explaining recommended work in a way customers can understand
- Keeping customers updated throughout the repair and servicing process
- Discussing additional work and obtaining customer authorisation where required
- Explaining technical information without unnecessary jargon
- Advising customers on servicing, maintenance and future requirements
- Managing queries and resolving issues calmly and professionally
- Making sure vehicles are ready for collection and the handover is smooth
- Building strong customer relationships that encourage customers to return
- Working towards customer satisfaction, departmental and commercial KPIs
- Following dealership and manufacturer processes accurately

What we're looking for

We're looking for someone who understands that great Service Advising is about more than booking cars in and handing over keys.

You'll need to be confident with customers, commercially aware and organised enough to keep control when the workshop gets busy.

You'll ideally have:
- Previous experience as a Service Advisor within an automotive dealership
- A good understanding of workshop and aftersales operations
- Excellent communication skills, both face-to-face and over the phone
- Confidence discussing recommended and additional work with customers
- Strong organisation and attention to detail
- The ability to manage competing priorities without losing sight of the customer
- A proactive approach to problem solving
- A positive, professional and team-focused attitude
- A full UK driving licence

Franchised dealership experience would be advantageous, but it isn't everything. If you have strong automotive customer service experience and the right approach, we're happy to have a conversation.

What's on offer
- £28,000 basic salary
- £33,000 OTE
- Established automotive dealership
- Supportive aftersales environment
- Training and development opportunities
- Long-term career progression
- The opportunity to build on your automotive experience within an established team

Let's talk

If you're an experienced Service Advisor in or around Cheltenham and you're open to hearing about something new, we'd like to hear from you.

You don't have to be actively looking.

If you're curious about the role, we'll give you the full picture, answer your questions honestly and let you decide whether it's right for you.

No pressure. No hard sell. Just a straightforward conversation about the opportunity and what you're looking for next.

Apply today or let us know you are interested for a confidential conversation with Pembrook Resourcing.

Please note: dealership details will be discussed confidentially with suitable candidates during the recruitment process.

title: Credit Controller
description:
Robert Half are working in partnership with a reputable, continuously growing company in Cirencester to recruit a Credit Controller role on a full-time permanent basis. This is a great opportunity for a proactive and organised Credit Controller to join their Finance team. This role is key to reducing outstanding debt, supporting company policies, improving cash flow, and ensuring timely payment collection while maintaining strong customer relationships. The successful candidate will be responsible for managing customer accounts, resolving payment queries efficiently, and providing vital support to the wider Finance function and business growth. The salary is up to £30,000 plus hybrid working and other excellent benefits.

The Role

The main duties of the role will consist of:
- Chase outstanding payments by telephone and email, agree payment dates, and maintain accurate records of customer conversations.
- Managing debtor communications in line with company credit control policy, including sending reminder letters, copy invoices, and proof of delivery documents.
- Issuing sales invoices and credit notes to maintenance customers and submit invoices and credits through customer portals.
- Posting cash receipts accurately and carry out general customer account administration, including credit account applications.
- Liaising closely with Sales Teams to resolve customer queries and disputes promptly while maintaining positive customer relationships.
- Processing credit checks, report on debtor status to the Assistant Finance Manager, and provide cover across Accounts Receivable and other finance functions as needed.

About you

To be considered for the Credit Controller role, you must ideally possess the following skills/experience:
- Must have 2+ years within credit control or accounts receivable.
- Confident communicating with customers by phone and email.
- Highly organised with strong attention to detail.
- Able to manage queries and disputes professionally and efficiently.
- Comfortable working collaboratively with internal stakeholders.
- Able to prioritise workload and meet deadlines in a fast-paced environment.

Salary & Benefits
- £28,000 - £30,000 annual salary
- Hybrid working; 2 days from home, 3 days on site
- Pension scheme
- 25 days annual leave
- Life assurance
- On site parking

title: Data Protection Co-Ordinator
company: Marley Risk Consultants Limited - Agency - Permanent
description:
Data Protection Co-Ordinator

Location: Cheltenham / Hybrid

Salary: £30-35k

What You'll Be Doing

Working alongside the Data Protection Officer, you'll support Marley Risk Consultants in meeting its obligations under the UK GDPR and Data Protection Act 2018. You'll co-ordinate Data Subject Access Requests, maintain accurate data protection records and registers, support Data Protection Impact Assessments and monitor the Data Protection inbox.

You'll help ensure requests, enquiries and potential incidents are logged, progressed and retained correctly. Working across the business, you'll gather information securely, monitor statutory deadlines, identify gaps or risks and escalate urgent, sensitive or higher-risk matters promptly to the Data Protection Officer.

This is a great opportunity for someone who is highly organised, detail-focused and confident handling sensitive information. You'll combine practical data protection knowledge with strong administration and communication skills, helping maintain a clear audit trail and a consistent approach to privacy compliance.

Key Responsibilities:
- Support the day-to-day administration of Data Subject Access Requests, ensuring requests are logged accurately, statutory deadlines are tracked, a clear audit trail is maintained and risks of delay are escalated.
- Work with teams across the organisation to identify and gather information required for DSAR responses using approved systems and secure handling methods.
- Review documents and identify information that may require redaction or exemption, referring final decisions and approval to the Data Protection Officer.
- Assist with reviewing DSAR material and preparing accurate, complete and timely responses for approval.
- Maintain accurate data protection logs and registers, including the personal data breach log, DPIA register and DSAR log, checking for missing, overdue or inconsistent entries.
- Monitor and manage the Data Protection inbox by triaging correspondence, recording actions, assigning or escalating matters and retaining completed items appropriately.
- Identify urgent, sensitive or higher-risk matters, including potential personal data breaches, complaints, regulatory correspondence and requests approaching statutory deadlines.
- Prepare complete case folders, check them against relevant records and promptly notify the Data Protection Officer of missing information, correspondence or actions.
- Support the initial recording and assessment of suspected personal data breaches, ensuring relevant information is captured and escalated in line with procedure.
- Support routine data protection queries, staff guidance, awareness activities and DPIAs, referring matters requiring formal advice or decision-making to the Data Protection Officer.

What We're Looking For:

We're looking for someone who can manage detailed administrative processes, protect confidential information and keep accurate records while working to statutory deadlines. You'll be methodical, proactive and comfortable working independently within agreed procedures, with the judgement to recognise when escalation is required.

Experience
- Practical knowledge of the UK GDPR, the Data Protection Act 2018 and secure personal data handling principles.
- Experience supporting or managing DSARs, including logging, information gathering, review, redaction, deadline monitoring and preparation of responses.
- Experience handling sensitive and confidential information securely within organisational systems.
- Experience supporting the recording, initial assessment and escalation of suspected personal data breaches and contributing to DPIAs.
- Experience working across business areas to obtain, review and organise information within agreed timescales.
- Experience using Microsoft 365 or similar case and document-management systems to maintain accurate records, actions and audit trails.

Skills & Expertise

You'll bring:
- Strong organisational and administrative skills, excellent attention to detail and the ability to prioritise competing deadlines.
- Clear and professional written and verbal communication skills.
- Practical understanding of DSAR administration, secure information handling, redaction principles, statutory deadline monitoring and accurate record keeping.
- Confidence using Microsoft 365 and associated workflow tools.
- The ability to work independently within agreed procedures and recognise when formal advice or escalation is required.
- A discreet, dependable and collaborative approach to sensitive information and stakeholder relationships.
- Knowledge of DPIAs, records of processing activities, personal data breach management and ICO guidance is desirable.

Why Join Marley Risk Consultants?

At Marley, we're passionate about creating an environment where our people can make an impact, develop their expertise and help shape the way we work.

This is an opportunity to build practical experience across a broad range of data protection activity while supporting a function that protects individuals, strengthens governance and enables responsible business decisions. You'll be encouraged to contribute ideas, improve processes and help embed good data protection practice across the organisation.

You'll be joining a collaborative business where your voice matters, with opportunities to learn, develop and build your career alongside people committed to doing the right thing.

If you're looking for a role where you can make a difference, take ownership and support a strong culture of privacy and accountability, we'd love to hear from you.

Salary: £32,000 to £35,000 per annum
Location: Quenington, Gloucestershire, GL7 5 BN
Hours: Full time, 35 hours per week
Closing date: Wednesday 18 November 2026
First interviews: Wednesday 2 December 2026 via Microsoft Teams
Second interviews: Thursday 10 or Friday 11 December 2026 in Quenington

About the role

This varied role offers the opportunity to put your organisational skills to work supporting the management of rural estates, land and property, while contributing to a charity that connects people with nature.

Working closely with the Director of Land, Property and Commercial Development and the wider team, you will keep schedules, projects and priorities on track. You will build relationships with colleagues and external contacts, providing reliable support across estate management and development activities.

Key responsibilities include:
- Managing busy diaries, meetings and communications, responding to changing priorities.
- Coordinating travel, accommodation, site visits and events.
- Supporting reporting cycles, governance processes and team initiatives.
- Recording and tracking actions, decisions and commitments.
- Acting as a key point of contact for colleagues and external stakeholders.
- Maintaining accurate records and structured digital filing systems.
- Improving administrative processes and making effective use of digital tools.
- Handling confidential and commercially sensitive information with discretion.

About you

You will be a professional, methodical and adaptable coordinator who enjoys bringing order to a busy workload. You will use your initiative, anticipate what needs doing and stay calm when priorities change.

You will bring:
- Experience within property, land or estate environments, preferably in the rural sector.
- Experience supporting managers with operational delivery and wider priorities.
- Strong communication and relationship-building skills.
- Confidence using Microsoft 365 and other digital tools.
- Excellent attention to detail and the judgement to prioritise, redirect or escalate matters appropriately.
- A collaborative, practical and solutions-focused approach.

Applications are welcomed from people with a range of relevant skills and experience. You do not need experience across every aspect of the role.

About the organisation

This educational charity helps people build meaningful connections with land and nature. Through outdoor learning, grant-making, partnerships and progressive land management, it supports opportunities for people across the UK to learn, develop and thrive.

Benefits include a 10% employer pension contribution, 27 days' annual leave plus bank holidays and additional leave between Christmas and New Year, life assurance, an Employee Assistance Programme and a personal training budget.

To apply, please submit your CV and a covering letter explaining your suitability. Appointment is subject to satisfactory background checks and proof of the right to work in the UK. The role may close early if sufficient applications are received.
